# core/p256.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/p256.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

ECDSA signatures over the curve P-256 (secp256r1) with
SHA-256, verification only (FIPS 186-4, RFC 6979 is for signing), for the
ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256 scheme of TLS 1.3 certificates.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, and the numbers
the arithmetic works on have 16 limbs. Not proved: that the arithmetic is
right; the tests check signatures made by OpenSSL, many one-bit changes of
the signature, key and message being refused, and out-of-range values. The
code is not constant time and does not need to be: verification handles
only public values.

A number is a `Vec[u64]` of 16 limbs of 16 bits, least significant first,
below 2^256. Products are built by doubling and adding, which is slow (a
verification takes about as long as a few thousand field multiplications of
256 steps each) but short enough to read.

`import "core/p256.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/der.bastio](core-der.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/sha256.bastio](core-sha256.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`ecdsa_p256_verify`](#ecdsa_p256_verify) | Whether `sig` is a valid ECDSA signature of `msg` under the public key `pubkey`, with the curve P-256 and SHA-256. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `Modulus`

```bastio
struct Modulus { m: Vec[u64], r2: Vec[u64], minv: u64 }
```

Internal: a prime modulus `m` with what Montgomery multiplication needs:
`r2` is 2^512 modulo `m` and `minv` is -1/m modulo 2^16.

### `P256Point`

```bastio
struct P256Point { x: Vec[u64], y: Vec[u64], z: Vec[u64] }
```

Internal: a point in Jacobian coordinates, (X / Z^2, Y / Z^3); Z = 0 is
the point at infinity.

## Functions

### `ecdsa_p256_verify`

```bastio
fn ecdsa_p256_verify(pubkey: &Bytes, msg: &Bytes, sig: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires blen(msg) < 274877906944 && blen(sig) < 274877906944 && blen(pubkey) < 274877906944
```

Whether `sig` is a valid ECDSA signature of `msg` under the public key
`pubkey`, with the curve P-256 and SHA-256. `pubkey` is the 65 bytes of
an uncompressed point (0x04, x, y) and `sig` the DER encoding of
SEQUENCE { INTEGER r, INTEGER s } that X.509 and TLS use. A key that is
not on the curve, an `r` or `s` outside 1..n-1 and any other encoding are
refused.

Example:

```bastio
let key = balloc(65);
let msg = bfrom("hello");
let sig = balloc(8);
let ok = ecdsa_p256_verify(key, msg, sig);
bfree(sig);
bfree(msg);
bfree(key);
if ok { return 1; }
```

## Specification functions

### `mod_ok`

```bastio
spec fn mod_ok(m: &Modulus) -> bool {
  vlen(m.m) == 16 && vlen(m.r2) == 16
}
```

Internal: the modulus has 16 limbs, like its `r2`.

## Internals

### `p256_nib`

```bastio
fn p256_nib(c: u8) -> u64
  ensures result < 16
```

Internal: the value of the hex digit `c` (0 for anything else).

### `bn_zero`

```bastio
fn bn_zero() -> Vec[u64]
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the number 0.

### `bn_copy`

```bastio
fn bn_copy(a: &Vec[u64]) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: a copy of `a`.

### `bn_small`

```bastio
fn bn_small(v: u64) -> Vec[u64]
  requires v < 65536
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the number `v` (below 65536).

### `bn_hex`

```bastio
fn bn_hex(s: Str) -> Vec[u64]
  requires slen(s) == 64
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the number written as the 64 hex digits of `s`.

### `bn_from_bytes`

```bastio
fn bn_from_bytes(b: &Bytes, at: u64) -> Vec[u64]
  requires at + 32 <= blen(b) && at < 274877906944
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the big-endian number in the 32 bytes `b[at..at+32]`.

### `bn_ge`

```bastio
fn bn_ge(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64]) -> bool
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16
```

Internal: whether `a >= b`.

### `bn_eq`

```bastio
fn bn_eq(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64]) -> bool
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16
```

Internal: whether `a == b`.

### `bn_is_zero`

```bastio
fn bn_is_zero(a: &Vec[u64]) -> bool
```

```bastio

  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16
  ensures vlen(result) == 17
```

### `mod_add`

```bastio
fn mod_add(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64], m: &Modulus) -> Vec[u64]
```


### `p256_double`

```bastio
fn p256_double(q: &P256Point, p: &Modulus) -> P256Point
  requires vlen(q.x) == 16 && vlen(q.y) == 16 && vlen(q.z) == 16 && mod_ok(p)
```

### `p256_add`

```bastio
fn p256_add(q1: &P256Point, q2: &P256Point, p: &Modulus) -> P256Point
  requires vlen(q1.x) == 16 && vlen(q1.y) == 16 && vlen(q1.z) == 16
  requires vlen(q2.x) == 16 && vlen(q2.y) == 16 && vlen(q2.z) == 16 && mod_ok(p)
  ensures vlen(result.x) == 16 && vlen(result.y) == 16 && vlen(result.z) == 16
```

Internal: `q1 + q2`.

### `p256_mul`

```bastio
fn p256_mul(k: &Vec[u64], q: &P256Point, p: &Modulus) -> P256Point
  requires vlen(k) == 16 && vlen(q.x) == 16 && vlen(q.y) == 16 && vlen(q.z) == 16 && mod_ok(p)
  ensures vlen(result.x) == 16 && vlen(result.y) == 16 && vlen(result.z) == 16
```

### `p256_on_curve`

```bastio
fn p256_on_curve(x: &Vec[u64], y: &Vec[u64], p: &Modulus) -> bool
  requires vlen(x) == 16 && vlen(y) == 16 && mod_ok(p)
```

Internal: whether (x, y) is on the curve y^2 = x^3 - 3x + b, with both
coordinates below `p`.

### `p256_der_uint`

```bastio
fn p256_der_uint(sig: &Bytes, start: u64, end: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires start <= end && end <= blen(sig)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 32
```

Internal: the signature number in the INTEGER `item` of `sig` as 32
bytes, if it is a positive DER integer of at most 256 bits in the shortest
form.

### `p256_verify_numbers`

```bastio
fn p256_verify_numbers(qx: &Vec[u64], qy: &Vec[u64], e: &Vec[u64], r: &Vec[u64], s: &Vec[u64]) -> bool
  requires vlen(qx) == 16 && vlen(qy) == 16 && vlen(e) == 16 && vlen(r) == 16 && vlen(s) == 16
```

Internal: checks the signature (`r`, `s`) of the hash `e` under the key
(`qx`, `qy`), all as numbers.
